65.t: The cooperative band for Panama that never went
65.s: Machito and Mario formed a band with Panchito Riset, Miguelito Valdes and others, rehearsed, but the Panama contract failed.
65.ch: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
65.q: Yeah. The only thing - the only older one was Arcelon Perez, that he lives in Mexico now, and Poligemo the bass player. The rest, Miguelito Valdes the violin --, he was about his early twanties, the rest was a bunch of young guys.

65.t: Joining Maria Teresa Vera's septeto as maraca player
65.s: After 1926 Mario worked at casinos while Machito played maracas with Maria Teresa Vera; he got the job through Miguelito Garcia.
65.ch: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
65.q: 1926? Well, Mario was working with Jose Curbelo's father at the Summer Casino for two years and then he worked at The Montmatre.

65.s: He joined Barroso's Agabama with Cheo Marquetti and Felix Chapotin, playing son montuno, which he says is now called salsa.
65.ch: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
65.q: The Agabama was Barroso, Cheo Marqueti, the bongo player, the guitar player, the tres player and Chapotin in the trumpet.

65.s: Clarifying dates, he explains he replaced a maraca player at Sexteto Nacional, then moved to Maria Teresa and then Agabama, and talks of Alfredito Valdes.
65.q: Nacional? From 1929 to about six months with the Sexteto Nacional, because Bienvenido Leon, he don't know how to play the maracas, he was a singer, beautiful baritone voice, and they need a maraca player because a sextet/is very important instrument. So in account that they saw me playing at the…

558.t: Montparnasse, Jovenes Sociales, Apolo and Bolero del 35
558.s: He lists successive groups and instruments (Montparnasse on bass, Jovenes Sociales on guitar, Apolo on tres, then Tata Gutierrez's Bolero) and the members of Septeto Apolo.
558.q: From that time, there was Gloria Habanera. Then there was, the group, the Septeto Montparnasse. I don’t remember the musicians well, the names, because well you know so many years, but I remember the Montparnasse as it was called. After the Gloria Habanera I worked with the Montparnasse.

558.t: From amateur septets to the Havana cabarets
558.s: He moves from a bought pawn-shop flute to amateur septets (Gloria Habanera, Jovenes del Cerro, Apolo with Mongo Santamaria), Nacional Juvenil with Vicentico Valdes, then Kursaal and Tropicana in 1942-43.
558.q: It was like that. Well, then he bought me a professional one. But not new, he did not buy it new. He bought one used as we say, in what they call, a pawn shop.

798.t: First band: the pupils' yard band
798.s: The first band was a group of Perkins's pupils who played in his yard on Sundays. Clark lists the members.
798.q: Well the first band I ever played in, the boys that were taking lessons there, we set up a little brass band just amongst us scholars. And he'd take us one Sunday evening in the yard. He'd sit us in his yard. And that's how we started playing. Every other Sunday we would go and we'd sit in that…

261.t: Playing around town with Red Allen and young local bands
261.s: Verrett says he never played with Red Allen when young, but led small spot bands with Albert Wallace and Camille Robinson.
261.q: Well, during the time he was down there playing, his dad was strict on him. He used to play, he had his band. I used to spot a different band, Walter, Albert Wallace, and Camille Robinson, we used to all have a little band and spot here and there. That's when Allen was here, that's years ago when…

266.t: The Dixie Cats and the musicians on Jones's first gig
266.s: Jones names the likely first-gig band, including Eddie Winston, Sonny Gammond and the Alexis brothers, one of whom played string bass.
266.q: That was D-I-X-I-E-C-A-T-S. Oh no, it was one word. One word? D-I-X-I-E-C-A-T-S.

601.t: Founding the Rika band with Willie Parker and Boogerman
601.s: Martin describes where the band first rehearsed, how he found a trombonist for Willie Parker in the person of Boogerman, and how Willie Parker came to play bass.
601.ch: The Rika band and funeral bands
601.q: they live in that to own 919 St. Gloria Street St. Gloria Street that's where Waterboy and Willie Parker and them started that band right there that's right with this fella used to cut hair back there used to have a barber shop there 1515 Bianco Street I forget his name now he used to wear a red…

403.t: When Bolden formed his band and Manuel Hall's role
403.s: Bolden started his own band around 1900, called Bolden's Band. Manuel Hall had no band of his own.
403.q: He was just a carnage player. I didn't know nothin' about him happening. Mm-hmm. Now the whole time I know that maybe I had before I come here. But he'll set up man when I first come here. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.

799.t: A small band with Eddie Miller and the Millers
799.s: He joined a six-piece band with Eddie Miller, Benny and Lloyd Miller, Irving Kero and Joe Harris, playing country-town jobs.
799.q: Then I got in with a little band with Eddie Miller and the other fellas, three Millers in the band, none of them related.

724.t: Early small band with Johnny Deve and Henry Landry
724.s: His first band was a six-piece group with Deve and Landry, lasting about a year.
724.q: There was six pieces. There were six pieces in that band. That's about the only ones I remember. Johnny Deve and Landry on trumpet.

664.t: His first bands: Durfee, Hilton Lamare, Lester Buchanan, Joe Klessy
664.s: He recounts his earliest groups from about age sixteen, then Klessy's six-piece band, and Cats urging him to join Brownlee.
664.q: what was the very first band you played with you said well the first band i played was joe clessy outside a little man i'm telling you about with frank durfey and uh his brother cat's mistress uh but the first uh i don't call that a band it was just a little full piece group but uh no after that i…

800.t: First jazz band with Paul Villar and Edgar Briscoe
800.s: He recalls the first band he organized with Paul Villar and guitar-banjo player Edgar Briscoe.
800.q: Yeah, he used to play banjo. He used to play banjo.

572.t: Forming the Six Nola Jazz and the Dixieland Rompers
572.s: He recalls his first band, its members, and the name change to Dixieland Rompers, first to broadcast live.
572.ch: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
572.q: And then played all the acts and everything else, you know? Mm-hmm. But he played good drums, and, and they had, uh, Kid René had a good drummer, too. I used to go and follow the bands all around, all these private parties, and every once in a while they let me sit in. When I first started to play…

194.t: First group and the Shuffling Hungarians
194.s: His early public work was amateur; the first group he formed included Robert Parker and a boy who claimed to be Hungarian, which gave the band its name.
194.q: Not my group, I was just with them. I worked with them. That's the first showing that I appeared with in the public. Mm-hmm. I was with them. Sonny Boyd Williams, we worked together at the New York Inn. Well I made appearance in front of people. Nothing professional.

290.t: Forming the Supreme Band with Eddie Jackson
290.s: His first trumpet band was the six-piece Supreme Band, organized with bass player Eddie Jackson, and it lasted a couple of years.
290.q: Oh, just Eddie and myself, we organized, you know, we got a couple of fellas together. You know some of these bands was organized and they last about, the organization would last about two months. But this band lasted longer than that. Oh yeah, that lasted for a couple of years, I think. And we had…

291.s: He began playing in a band at 17 and lists its members, though the ASR loops on one name.
291.q: Well, I started playing in a band actually in 1919. I was 17 years old and I was going on 18. I wouldn't be 18 in November of that year, in 1919, but I started playing a little before I got to my birthday so it actually made me start playing at 17. Oh that's pretty young.

766.t: Forming his own band with older musicians
766.s: He formed a band of his own with older men like Picou, Toca, Dominguez, Ike Roberson, and Boyd.
766.q: I had the old musicians with me. Really? That's right, I had old man granny, Alphonse Pico, Johnny Dave, Lil' Orange Toker, Gassoun, you remember Gassoun, you got to. I had all old musicians. Lil' Orange Toker and me was the two youngest fellas. I mostly worked with old fellas, I mean when I…

801.t: First band with Josiah, Lawrence and friends; Oil for Sale, 1924
801.s: The group Eddie started with is named: Josiah on drums, Raymond Brown on trombone, Bush Hall on cornet, Lawrence on banjo. They played together in 1924 before parting.
801.q: Well, we started together. It was Josiah on drum. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Raymond Brown on trambone. Bushall on the corner of his age. And, um, Lawrence on the bench. Oh yeah, Louis Conqueror was named. From a boy.

802.t: First band, the Ohio Lucky Seven, and jazz outside New Orleans
802.s: His first band in Defiance was the Ohio Lucky Seven; he argues fine jazz musicians came from places like Indiana, such as Bix.
802.q: My first band? Yeah Well, In Defiance, where I was born It was a very fine band too I mean, it really was a good jazz band for those days It was called the Ohio Lucky Seven And it's just too bad that we didn't record for Jeanette in those days Because we did have it down pretty good, you know And…

786.t: Starting out and forming the Memphis Jug Band
786.s: Shade's first paid group included Ben Ramey, Will Weldon and Elijah (Roundhouse); they became the Memphis Jug Band and made a first record.
786.q: Well, when I first started making money, I started in with Benny Ramey, Will Welton, myself, and another fella called Roundhouse. But his name was Elijah.

471.s: Cobb recalls his quartet with Frank Wess, pianist Rob Harley and a bassist, and a photo used on a CD.
471.ch: Growing up and learning drums in Washington
471.q: That’s probably right. I had a – I was in a band with Frank. We had a quartet. I was in his quartet. Recently he sent a photo that we had taken together, which was about – by the time I got it, it was about 50 years old. We’re looking [?]. We used it on one of our CDs that we put out – that Eleana…

460.t: The Afro-Classic Ensemble and its drummer Freddie Waits
460.s: Brown opens the LP; Laws recalls his first group, the Afro-Classic Ensemble, with Ron Carter and Freddie Waits.
460.ch: The Met orchestra and joining CTI
460.q: You hadn’t even opened it up.

382.t: Her uncle's Red Hot Peppers band and becoming a regular vocalist
382.s: She sang with her uncle's band, becoming regular vocalist around 1934.
382.ch: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
382.q: : There were two brothers, one played the piano and one played the drums, and their last name was Stafford. One was Frank, and I forget the other one's name and of course Jess, my cousin played the guitar along with them. And that
